*In progress.*

The history of community forestry in India is longstanding, yet today approximately [97% of forests in India are managed by the government](https://landconservationnetwork.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/India20Country20Profile20on20Privately20Protected20Areas_7_24_2019-1.pdf). Understanding the ecology of different management strategies could inform new ways of managing forests, especially in the age of climate change.

This is where computational modeling approaches become useful. We can simulate the actions of different management strategies (e.g. a community extracts firewood → removing biomass from a system) under different climate scenarios and take note of the responses we see in carbon and water dynamics. We aim to use [RHESSys](https://rhessys.github.io/) to do this kind of modeling work. 

#### Bren Environmental Leadership (BEL) Fellowship

But before we model anything, we need to narrow down which areas we want to study. RHESSys performs at the plot to catchment scale, so we need to decide which watersheds will make the cut, and also articulate why we think these watersheds are interesting.

This was the point I addressed during my summer in the BEL Fellowship Program. We ultimately selected 9 watersheds based on variables like forest cover, precipitation, temperature, and elevation. On top of that, we identified 30 environmental datasets related to climate, hydrology, vegetation, and soil to input into RHESSys for future modeling. 

In the end, I had the opportunity to recap my 10-week summer in 5 minutes at the Summer\@Bren Flash Talks.
